subject: Questions: EU-US data transfer / DPF & DPA annex — requested details
messages:
From: Albert Green <albert.green@medcore-health.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurements Team <procurements@medcore-health.com>, Liza Moreau <liza.moreau@medcore-health.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial privacy questionnaire items — EU/US transfer specifics

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's routing and cost controls. We're moving your proposal to our legal/privacy review and they have a handful of follow-ups specifically about cross-border transfers and the new EU Data Protection Framework (DPF) timeline. Can you confirm the following for us by EOD Friday?

1) Do you plan to adopt the new EU DPF adequacy mechanism and on what target date?
2) For EU-origin personal data that flows to the U.S., do you rely on SCCs, DPF, or a mix?
3) We need a completed mapping that shows subprocessors in the U.S. and whether transfer protections are applied end-to-end (e.g., encryption, contractual terms).
4) If our data is processed on Dedicated capacity in AWS eu-west-1, does any metadata still route to U.S. control plane or analytics services?

We're attaching the privacy team template — filling points 2 and 3 in particular will help speed procurement.

Appreciate a clear callout of any open items where you need our legal to accept alternative language.

Best,
Albert
Procurement Manager
MedCore Health

Attachment: medcore_privacy_template_questions.docx (docx)
From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Albert Green <albert.green@medcore-health.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Mar 2026 14:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial privacy questionnaire items — EU/US transfer specifics

Hi Albert — thanks for sending this over and for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (acct exec) and Vivek (security & privacy) so we can provide a concise package. We're preparing:

- A short DPA annex (v2) that maps processing roles and subprocessors (attached).
- An SCC/DPF mapping matrix indicating which legal mechanism applies per transfer.
- A brief note on control plane telemetry and metadata handling.

Quick answers up-front:
- Redwood intends to adopt the EU DPF once the adequacy instrument is formally adopted; target is Q3 2026 subject to final guidance (we will update when certified).
- For current customers we rely primarily on SCCs + contractual DPA annex; we will offer DPF-based transfers for customers who require it once available.
- Dedicated capacity customers can opt for regionally pinned deployments; the control plane may call home to a U.S.-hosted management endpoint for billing/telemetry unless you choose Private deployment. We will document the exact telemetry fields.

We'll aim to get the filled template and attachments to you by Thursday COB. If you want a quick call to walk through the matrix, propose a time and we'll join.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood_dpa_annex_v2.pdf (pdf)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Albert Green <albert.green@medcore-health.com>, neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, jordan_blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Mar 2026 09:27:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial privacy questionnaire items — EU/US transfer specifics

Hi Albert, Neha —

Appended the mapping spreadsheet you requested (SCC mapping matrix) and a short summary below. High-level points:

- Current posture: SCCs + standard Redwood DPA annex. For customers on Dedicated we support region pinning of model execution and data-at-rest in the selected region.
- Control plane: Minimal telemetry needed for billing and autoscaling decisions does transit Redwood's U.S. control plane. We can provide a filtered list of telemetry fields and propose options to minimize them (e.g., no user identifiers, only boolean flags and aggregated metrics).
- Encryption: Data in transit and at rest is encrypted (TLS 1.2+/AES-256). Customer-managed keys (via KMS integration) are available for Private and Dedicated Private installs.
- Subprocessors: The attached matrix lists subprocessors, their country, and legal basis for transfer. We maintain subprocessors' contracts to include SCC terms, and we offer an annexed subprocessors list for procurement.

Open items for MedCore:
- Confirm whether you require the control plane to be located in the EU (Private offering) or if filtered telemetry to U.S. is acceptable.
- Confirm whether you want Data Protection Impact Assessment (DPIA) artifacts and independent audit reports (SOC2 Type II) attached to the RFP packet.

If helpful, Jordan (legal) can provide redlineable language for the DPA annex on transfer mechanisms.

Regards,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Security & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: scc_mapping_matrix.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Albert Green <albert.green@medcore-health.com>
To: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>

Date: Fri, 20 Mar 2026 11:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial privacy questionnaire items — EU/US transfer specifics

Thanks Vivek — that's helpful. A few follow-ups from privacy:

- We need explicit confirmation that when MedCore chooses Dedicated capacity in eu-west-1, no user-level personal data will be accessible by Redwood staff outside the EU without an additional lawful basis. Is this achieved via encryption + key control, or do you rely on contractual limits plus SCCs?
- For the telemetry fields, please provide the exact list you mentioned so our privacy team can evaluate.
- MedCore's legal prefers DPF-based transfers if available; please keep us updated on the vendor timeline. For now, we will accept SCCs if the subprocessors mapping and contractual protections are complete.

Can Jordan or someone in legal provide the redlineable DPA annex language for our counsel to review? Also, please include an estimated turnaround for any custom DPA redline review (we typically expect 7–10 business days).

Appreciate the quick responses.

Best,
Albert

Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2026 16:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Initial privacy questionnaire items — EU/US transfer specifics

Albert —

Following up with the redlineable language. Attached is a DPA annex excerpt that explicitly states:

- For Dedicated region-pinned deployments, Redwood will process customer content in the selected region and any access by Redwood staff outside of that region requires approval and is limited to incident response where necessary; access is logged and audited.
- If customer requests customer-managed keys, Redwood will not retain plaintext keys; key material remains under customer KMS control unless otherwise agreed.
- For the present contract cycle we rely on SCCs; DPF adoption will be added as an amendment once the EU instrument is finalized.

Estimated review timeline: standard redline cycle 7–10 business days from receipt of customer edits; if MedCore requires bespoke legal terms outside the DPA annex, that may extend review depending on corporate legal sign-off.

Next steps for us:
- Neha to share the finalized filled privacy template to procurements.
- Vivek to export the telemetry field list and the subprocessors CSV.
- Jordan to post the DPA annex excerpt to the shared drive and mark items that are likely to be negotiated.

Happy to hop on a brief call if you want to walk counsel through the language.

Regards,
Jordan Blake
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
